bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` in the staged HarfBuzz checkout `a975ec4842468e574484bdc310095fad780978fc`. On the crashing path, `glyph_for_gid()` materializes a `Glyph` as an `hb_bytes_t` slice into the attacker-controlled `glyf` table. Inside `_populate_subset_glyphs()`, the loop walks `plan->glyph_map->iter()` in `hb_map` hash-table iteration order, stores the current glyph state in `glyphs[new_gid]`, and increments `idx` only after a successful `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` return. Because the saved PoC's subset flags decode to `0`, `HB_SUBSET_FLAGS_NO_HINTING` is clear and the current loop iteration first assigns `subset_glyph.dest_start = subset_glyph.source_glyph.get_bytes()`, leaving that slot as a borrowed alias of source-font bytes. On the reproduced witness, `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` then fails before `Glyph::compile_bytes_with_deltas()` reaches its later owned-buffer rewrites of `dest_start`, so the current `glyphs[new_gid].dest_start` stays borrowed. The crash stack shows the cleanup call at `src/OT/glyf/glyf.hh:437` executed, so `!plan->pinned_at_default && idx > 0` was true; because successfully compiled earlier glyphs would already have replaced `dest_start` with owned or empty bytes, the observed bad-free implies this failing iteration's `new_gid` already lay inside cleanup range `0..idx-1`. `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs()` therefore reaches the current failed slot while it still aliases source-font memory. The vulnerable `SubsetGlyph::free_compiled_bytes()` has no ownership bit and unconditionally runs `dest_start.fini()`, so `hb_array_t::fini()` passes the borrowed glyph pointer to `hb_free()`. ASan reports that freed address as 4660 bytes inside the 4844-byte libFuzzer testcase allocation, confirming that HarfBuzz freed source-font memory rather than HarfBuzz-owned heap storage. The metadata `patch.diff` is unrelated to this path; the relevant upstream fix is local history commit `3d05b96181b259593047f592df4df33a3658e472`, which adds `bool allocated` and frees only truly compiled glyph buffers.

source.code:
glyf_impl::Glyph glyph (hb_bytes_t ((const char *) this->glyf_table + start_offset,
                             end_offset - start_offset), gid);
source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that materializes a glyph's bytes as a borrowed `hb_bytes_t` slice of the attacker-controlled `glyf` table.
source.value_from: The slice points into the font blob built from the saved 4844-byte `poc`. ASan later reports the freed pointer as 4660 bytes inside that same testcase allocation, so one such borrowed glyph slice is the source of the invalid-free value.
source.note: `start_offset` and `end_offset` come from attacker-controlled `loca` entries. The exact crashing glyph id and offsets are not recoverable from the saved artifacts, but this is the source statement that creates the later-freed non-owned byte view.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `hb_free()` is called on `dest_start.arrayZ`, which still points into the testcase-backed font buffer instead of to HarfBuzz-owned heap storage.
sink.note: ASan reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed: 0x621000004f34`; that address is 4660 bytes inside the 4844-byte libFuzzer input allocation.

root_cause.description: `SubsetGlyph` does not track whether `dest_start` owns heap memory. `free_compiled_bytes()` therefore unconditionally frees `dest_start`, even when it is only a borrowed alias of source glyph bytes.
root_cause.note: The later upstream fix adds `bool allocated` and guards both `dest_start.fini()` and `dest_end.fini()` with that ownership bit. In the staged vulnerable source, no such check exists here, so cleanup of the failing `glyphs[new_gid]` slot still frees a borrowed alias.

parser_admitted.description: The run has already been admitted through face creation, subset planning, and `glyf` dispatch, and is now materializing per-glyph source bytes on the reproduced vulnerable path.

instancing_cleanup.description: The saved crash stack reaches line 437, proving that the run entered the instancing-only `if (font)` path, that `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` failed for the current glyph, and that the `!plan->pinned_at_default && idx > 0` cleanup call executed.

tainted_value_origin.description: The pointer later freed is first stored in the current `glyphs[new_gid]` slot here as a borrowed alias of `source_glyph.bytes`, not as compiled storage owned by HarfBuzz.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved PoC footer decodes `flags = 0`, so `HB_SUBSET_FLAGS_NO_HINTING` is clear and `_populate_subset_glyphs()` takes this direct-alias assignment instead of `drop_hints_bytes()`. `source_glyph.get_bytes()` returns the same input-backed `hb_bytes_t` slice materialized in source step 1.
tainted_value_origin.note: This assignment gives the current loop iteration its non-owned `dest_start.arrayZ`. The witness only becomes a bad-free because the same slot later fails `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` before any owned rewrite and is then swept by cleanup when `new_gid < idx`.

coarse_trace.summary: The subsetter materializes a glyph as a borrowed slice of the testcase-backed `glyf` table, assigns it to the current `glyphs[new_gid]` slot, and with `HB_SUBSET_FLAGS_NO_HINTING` clear stores that borrowed slice directly in `dest_start`.

On the crashing iteration, `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` fails before the current slot's borrowed `dest_start` is replaced with owned compiled/header bytes, while `idx` still counts only prior successful iterations.

Because loop order comes from `glyph_map->iter()` rather than numeric `new_gid` order, the failing `glyphs[new_gid]` slot can already lie inside cleanup range `0..idx-1`, so `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs()` reaches that still-borrowed slot.
Because `free_compiled_bytes()` unconditionally runs `dest_start.fini()`, `hb_free()` is reached on a pointer inside the libFuzzer testcase buffer, matching the saved ASan bad-free.

fine_trace.code:
glyf_impl::Glyph glyph (hb_bytes_t ((const char *) this->glyf_table + start_offset,
                             end_offset - start_offset), gid);
fine_trace.note: Source. Using `loca`-derived offsets, `glyph_for_gid()` wraps bytes from the attacker-controlled `glyf` table in an `hb_bytes_t` without copying them. ASan later shows the freed pointer still lies inside the 4844-byte testcase allocation, so one such borrowed slice is the ultimate source of the bad-free value.

The current glyph is stored in slot `glyphs[new_gid]`, but cleanup later uses `idx`, which starts at 0 and increases only after a successful compile. `plan->glyph_map->iter()` is `hb_map` iteration over internal hash-table items rather than numeric `new_gid` order, so a later failing iteration can already have `new_gid < idx`.
The borrowed `Glyph` from step 1 is stored in the current `glyphs[new_gid]` slot as `subset_glyph.source_glyph`.

Because the saved PoC's subset flags decode to `0`, `HB_SUBSET_FLAGS_NO_HINTING` is clear and `_populate_subset_glyphs()` copies `source_glyph.bytes` directly into `dest_start`. The current `glyphs[new_gid].dest_start` now aliases input-backed glyph bytes; no allocation occurs here.

On the witness, this call returns false for the current slot. The exact failure site inside `Glyph::compile_bytes_with_deltas()` is not recoverable from the saved artifacts, but the false return means the later successful rewrites at `Glyph.hh:212-239` did not complete for this slot, so `glyphs[new_gid].dest_start` still holds the borrowed alias from step 4.

The saved crash stack shows this cleanup call executed, so `!plan->pinned_at_default && idx > 0` was true. `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs(glyphs, idx - 1)` frees slots `0..idx-1`; because successfully compiled earlier glyphs would already have replaced `dest_start` with owned or empty bytes, the witnessed bad-free implies this failing iteration already had `new_gid < idx`, bringing the current still-borrowed slot into the cleanup range.
Cleanup iterates from `i = 0` through `i = idx - 1` and, on the witness, reaches `i = new_gid`, i.e. the current failed slot whose `dest_start` is still the borrowed alias from step 4.

Root cause. `free_compiled_bytes()` assumes `dest_start` is owned compiled storage and immediately calls `fini()` on it. The vulnerable `SubsetGlyph` has no ownership bit to distinguish this borrowed alias from an allocated buffer, so the failing slot from step 7 is freed as if it were owned.
Sink. `hb_array_t::fini()` calls `hb_free()` on `arrayZ`; here `arrayZ == dest_start.arrayZ` still points inside the testcase-backed font buffer, so ASan reports bad-free at `0x621000004f34`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated to the reproduced `src/OT/glyf` cleanup path. Local HarfBuzz history commit `3d05b96181b259593047f592df4df33a3658e472` fixes testcase `5388270411579392` by adding `bool allocated` to `SubsetGlyph` and freeing compiled glyph bytes only when they were actually allocated. Stage 02 did not run the fixed version, so `patch_resolves` remains false.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is libFuzzer's testcase buffer. The project-side root cause is later treating a borrowed slice of that external allocation as owned compiled glyph storage.

format.name: HarfBuzz subset-fuzzer sfnt + control footer
format.contract: A single fuzz input that is first parsed as a font blob by `hb_face_create()` and then, by the `hb-subset-fuzzer` harness, reinterpreted at the tail as 16 `hb_codepoint_t` values, a 32-bit `flags` word, a 32-bit `num_axes`, and zero or more `(int value, hb_tag_t tag)` axis records. For the saved 4844-byte witness, the decoded `flags` word is `0`, so the crashing loop iteration in `_populate_subset_glyphs()` takes `subset_glyph.dest_start = subset_glyph.source_glyph.get_bytes()` instead of hint-dropping. The reproduced crash further requires the same run to enter the instancing path and hit a failing `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` iteration whose current `new_gid` slot already lies inside cleanup range `0..idx-1`; only then does cleanup free a still-borrowed `dest_start` instead of a successfully recompiled glyph buffer.
